items.title: H33-2-B2 has no receipt-to-hash score attribution in this checkout
items.detail: The user/owner-supplied score attribution is not tied to the exact TIFF bytes or SHA-256 by an organizer submission receipt. The GEMSDOE32 owner page describes the artifact as unscored and states that no organizer score exists for its artifacts. Therefore neither the attribution nor a causal explanation is established. Do not promote owner prose or a public leaderboard row to a receipt.

items.title: Legacy emission eligibility uses distance to the full catalogue before holdout scoring
items.detail: scripts/run_h66.py computes distance from the full catalogue in load_state(), then uses that distance to restrict candidate cells in both s4_e2_holdout() and s4b_detector_holdout(). The hidden catalogue pixels therefore influence where predictions are allowed, even though the evaluator later hides them. The old holdout scalars are not leakage-clean and must not be reported as qualified HOLDOUT-DTI.

items.status: BLOCKED — legacy H66 entrypoint disabled; shared protocol integration still required
items.title: Legacy holdout is not the required buffered whole-geologic-segment, LiDAR-only instrument
items.detail: The legacy gems57 holdout builder chunks raster branches into at-most-12-pixel pieces and erodes quadrant boundaries; it does not guarantee whole authoritative geologic segments are withheld with a buffer. The shared gems.holdout API can select whole connected components in LiDAR-covered spatial blocks and apply a buffer, but absent authoritative segment IDs that is only a disclosed raster-component proxy. The H66 runner was disabled and does not call the valid-mask pooled evaluator with the required design/CI. Integrate the reviewed protocol once in the shared template; do not patch a private evaluator.

items.status: CORRECTED IN DOCUMENTATION; LEGACY FEATURES NOT QUALIFIED
items.title: Several H66 proxy fields were described as method-faithful Scarplet outputs
items.detail: In src/gems66/channels66.py, mean/max of two aggregate slope-excess bands is named a scarp-pixel fraction; the robust block z-score of an amplitude proxy is named template SNR; cross-face gradient divided by mean adjacent gradients is named morphologic relative age; and step_max multiplied by a fixed scale is named height. These are proxy constructions, not the published Scarplet template outputs. The owner-supplied 2 m stack/sidecar is not in the current checkout or organizer-authenticated. No current candidate may rely on those names as physical measurements.

items.status: LEGACY H66 PATH DISABLED — REWIRE TO CANONICAL SHARED WRITER
items.title: The vendored shared writer's all-finite export conflicts with the official NaN-outside contract
items.detail: The official problem description requires null/NaN outside the study bounds. The older gems57 grid/writer path enforces all-finite output, and the legacy H66 s5 path wrote TIFFs directly to docs/downloads. The canonical src/gems/submission_writer.py and validator support NaN-only outside a reference-grid footprint; H66 is not wired to that path. Reuse or correct the shared template integration and official-grid checks before re-enabling candidate generation; do not create a private fork.

items.title: The available raster registry is incomplete
items.detail: Prior local scans describe only the subset physically present in this checkout and explicitly mark the family corpus incomplete. No complete registry corpus or full pre-placement/final-dot scan is available in this review. Historical correlation or overlap results against a partial subset are not a uniqueness pass.

items.title: Official rasters and exact DEM-link inventory are absent
items.detail: The official data tab redirected to login; no credentials were used. The checkout has no competition rasters, sample grid, 1m_DEM_links.csv, shared cached stack, or existing cultural mask. USGS 3DEP offers public-domain 1 m bare-earth DEMs in principle, but this does not establish that the exact competition-area tiles are all available and aligned.

items.status: FIXED — no candidate file or download link is published
items.title: Historical pages advertised artifacts despite incomplete release gates
items.detail: Both site generators previously emitted direct TIFF/ZIP links and claimed download safety even though required reference/footprint checks were skipped and the registry was incomplete. The historical binaries remain removed from docs/downloads; byte-identical H66-1 copies are now preserved only in evidence/archives/h66-1/, outside the Pages document root and without site links. The withdrawal decision and hashes remain in the run card and audit record.

items.title: Generative-AI use must be disclosed in the official submission narrative when applicable
items.detail: The September 2026 official rules allow generative AI but require a narrative statement describing the extent and manner of its use in developing all submission elements. Add a truthful, specific disclosure to any future package; do not reuse a placeholder without editing it.

items.title: Independent scientific review has not been performed
items.detail: This is a single-agent repository/source audit. It is not two independent scientific-lead reviews. Obtain and preserve two separate reviews of the geology, mimics, holdout design, and feature interpretation before promotion.

items.status: NO AUTOMATED OR MANUAL STANDINGS MONITORING
items.title: DrivenData Terms of Use restrict monitoring/copying and subpage links
items.detail: The Terms of Use text read for this audit prohibits robots or other automated means and also manual monitoring/copying of website material without prior written consent; it also restricts links to subpages. The project's status feed therefore reports repository state only, stores no leaderboard rows, and performs no polling.

items.title: The previous fetch_inputs.sh claimed to restore files but did not copy them
items.detail: The old destination expression did not implement a reliable mapping from the template directory and the script exited on the missing destination rather than restoring it. It has been replaced with a local presence check that does not download, copy, or authenticate.

items.status: PRESERVED AS LEGACY EXPLORATORY NEGATIVE; NOT VALID HOLDOUT-DTI
items.title: Historical cultural-veto comparison used an SGMC-derived proxy, not competition truth
items.detail: The internal evidence bundle records a neutral-to-negative cultural-veto comparison using an SGMC-derived mapped-fault proxy. Its exact provenance is the historical H66 input/derived-layer manifest and evidence/h66_e1_offcat.json, not the unrelated GeoDAWN geophysical-survey record. The values are retained solely as unqualified exploratory evidence; the run uses the wrong holdout/valid-mask protocol and is not a competition score or a qualified HOLDOUT-DTI result.

items.title: The H66-2 stratum audit's first run used an index-ordered 'random' control
items.detail: scripts/h66b_strata.py drew its per-stratum random baseline with pick(np.ones(...)); argsort on a constant field returns cells in raster order, i.e. the top-left corner of the stratum, not a random sample. Every x-N-random ratio from that run was inflated roughly tenfold: the advertised x16 upland advantage of the H66-2 field is x1.20 against a uniform in-stratum baseline, and the incumbent's upland dots are x0.75, not x10. The corrected run replaces evidence/h66b_e2_strata.json; evidence/h66b_verdict.json carries the corrected ratios with the seed and the draw count.

items.title: scripts/stop_guard.py hard-coded a foreign lane name and failed closed on every runner here
items.detail: The guard tested for the lane name 'channel-steepness' from a sibling checkout before it would run anything, so in this repository (registered active_lane: native-resolution LiDAR scarp channels) it returned stop for every caller, including the measurement-only uniqueness audit, and it had no way to register a new hypothesis lane. It now takes an optional lane argument: callers scoped to a lane are blocked only by their own lane record, and legacy callers keep the original fail-closed default.

items.title: The portal's value check and the audit's NaN-outside contract disagree
items.detail: The audit's release gate requires NaN only outside the official footprint; the user-reported portal rejection 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' indicates the form rejects NaN-valued cells. The H66-2 artifact is therefore all-finite (0.0 outside the emitting cells, no nodata tag) and is reported as an all-finite variant. A NaN-outside twin can be produced only after the writer is rewired to the canonical shared writer, which the audit requires anyway. No artifact is published from either reading until the conflict is settled by an organizer receipt.

items.status: FIXED — audit-only bytes retained outside the Pages document root
items.title: Withdrawn H66-1 binaries are archived but remain unavailable for download
items.detail: The three historical TIFF/ZIP files were restored by identity under evidence/archives/h66-1/ after the newer main branch had removed them. SHA-256 hashes match the run card. The archive is not linked by the public site, does not restore release clearance, and does not change the known 62-of-655 registry limitation or unknown cause of the earlier portal range rejection.

items.status: BLOCKED — historical one-off pre-merge check; not current runner output
items.title: All nine required local input roles were absent in the one-off s0 check
items.detail: The session-branch s0 verifier exited 2 before loading data or starting an experiment; nine of nine roles were absent and pins were missing for external/lidar_scarp_features.json and external/topo_10m_derived_100m_u8.tif. The evidence was preserved at evidence/h66_inputs_s0_review.json. The newer main branch intentionally disables the legacy runner, so this snapshot is not a current preflight and cannot clear inputs.

items.status: FIXED IN THIS REPOSITORY; external template update not submitted
items.title: Continuous-surface and emitted-dot uniqueness need separate semantics
items.detail: The shared package previously conflated positive support on a dense detector surface with final emitted dots and could trust cached signed-only correlation flags. This branch now applies absolute Spearman plus exact pixel/hash identity in both phases, the 3-pixel overlap threshold only to emitted dots, and recomputes cached thresholds. The disabled legacy runner cannot use this code for release; external owner-template review/merge remains outstanding, so no upstream integration or complete registry clearance is claimed.

items.status: CORRECTED IN REPOSITORY; upstream snapshot/pin remains unverified
items.title: The prior shared-package provenance record overstated byte identity and referenced a missing pin
items.detail: The earlier record claimed 23/23 package files were identical and referred to registry/template_pin.json, but that pin file is absent from origin/main. After merging newer main and applying this PR, comparison to the stored per-file template_sha256 values finds 19/23 files identical; anatomy.py and metric.py differ in newer main, and uniqueness.py and gates.py are changed in this PR. No live upstream revision or tarball was fetched/verified, and no external template PR/merge is claimed. Keep the runner disabled and disclose the provenance limit.

items.status: OPEN — raw final-dot threshold trips; registry completeness is not certified
items.title: A density-adjusted uniqueness label cannot override the raw overlap stop or incomplete registry evidence
items.detail: The inherited lidar_lane final-dot comparison reports 0.990386 of candidate dots within 3 px of one accessible registry raster, above the stated >0.70 stop threshold; max absolute Spearman rho is 0.277125. A separate density-adjusted diagnostic labels the same scan UNIQUE, but the 1.5x random-placement lift is not an authorized exemption. Only 60 rasters were compared, no organizer-complete registry certificate or matching expected count is recorded, and pre-placement continuous-surface correlation is null/not reported. Pixel identity was not found in the accessible scan; a full registry file-hash/pixel agreement pass is not established. The candidate remains negative and not submission-cleared.

items.status: RESOLVED — conflicting paths reconciled and affected site pages regenerated
items.title: Incoming main conflicts overlapped PR #12's no-download site and audit changes
items.detail: Merging origin/main commit 8f522351 from merge-base 5970770b produced content conflicts in docs/downloads/README.md, docs/index.html, docs/irregularities.html, and scripts/build_site.py. The resolution preserves the no-download/audit-only state, combines the PR #12 provenance and raw-overlap disclosures with the current site generator, and regenerates affected HTML from repository data. This is a merge-process irregularity, not evidence that any scientific release gate passed.

items.title: sample_submission.tif and training_features.tif disagree on the footprint by 4,601 cells
items.detail: The finite mask of sample_submission.tif has 5,167,373 cells; band 1 of training_features.tif above the nodata sentinel has 5,165,852. Neither is a subset of the other: 1,540 cells are inside the features footprint but NaN in sample_submission, and 3,061 are finite in sample_submission but outside the features footprint. The writer now uses the features convention, which is what the shared validator and the reference solution use; if the organiser instead tests against the sample_submission mask, 1,540 cells would be NaN inside the expected area.

items.title: Frangi vesselness was numerically degenerate when c was estimated from image intensity
items.detail: Estimating Frangi's c as half the 99th percentile of the raw field intensity gave a maximum response of 0.0155 and a 99th percentile of 1.9e-4 over the whole footprint, i.e. the channel carried essentially no information. Fixed by estimating c from the pooled, sigma^2-normalised Hessian norm across all scales and by keeping the larger of the ridge and valley responses. The first experiment run used the defective channel; its numbers are superseded and retained in evidence/h66c_experiment1.json and h66c_experiment3.json.

items.title: The BLM closed-claim raster is an administrative status, not a disturbance mask
items.detail: 45% of the footprint lies within 150 m of a BLM closed claim, so a distance veto on that raster would remove most of the study area. 'Closed to mineral entry' does not imply any physical ground disturbance, so the term is disabled by default in scarp66.cultural_mask (claim_radius_m = 0).

items.title: No local holdout instrument is a validated surrogate for the hidden score
items.detail: Instrument N (SGMC off-catalogue, held blocks) correlates +0.644 (p = 0.0071) with the owner-reported live scores over 16 registry rasters, but rho(dots, live) is -0.844 on the same set and the partial correlation is not identified. Instrument S (withheld catalogue segments) correlates -0.708 (p = 0.0021): it measures rediscovery of the public catalogue, which the scored truth excludes by construction. The brief's gate can therefore not be met in any demonstrably predictive way. Any future session must establish an instrument whose correlation survives partialling out dot count before trusting a gain.

items.title: The catalogue-gap dose response rests on owner-reported scores, not organizer receipts
items.detail: The byte-level subset relation h33-2-b2 subset d28 (6,436 dots removed, all within 200.0 m of the catalogue) and the monotone -0.126-DTI-per-unit-f200 response across the d2-8 lineage are reproduced from the registry bytes, but the associated scores 0.2600 and 0.2778 are owner-reported. No organiser receipt ties either number to exact bytes.

items.title: The diffusion-inversion constants are defined only up to the upstream LoG normalisation
items.detail: The sidecar pins neither the LoG kernel nor its normalisation, so a_hat and kt_hat carry an unknown dimensionless constant. Both are used only through rank/percentile transforms, which are invariant to a positive constant; no absolute scarp height or age is claimed.

items.status: open — density-adjusted pass, literal raw rule trips
items.title: The literal >70% within-3 px duplicate rule trips on the H66-C candidate against a dense registry raster
items.detail: Raw maximum fraction of candidate dots within 3 px of one registry raster is 0.994, against gems61-lane-buried-step-gravinversion-hgm-r3-k400k-b2zeros.tif which carries 311,350 dots (6.0% of the footprint). Random placement already gives 0.958 against that raster, so the lift over random is 1.04x. Over the full 60-raster accessible set the maximum lift is 2.46x and the worst within-3 px fraction among the 48 rasters exceeding 1.5x random is 0.341, below the 0.70 stop. Rank correlation is at most |rho|=0.290. The literal rule therefore trips on density, not similarity (the same failure mode as IR-66-GATE-01). Following the stricter precedent set in IR-71 for the lidar_lane artifact, the density-adjusted UNIQUE verdict is reported explicitly as NOT overriding the raw rule; both numbers are shown on the site and in the run card. Full per-raster table: evidence/uniqueness_h66c_full.json.

items.title: Hand-edited Pages HTML was silently revertible by scripts/build_site.py
items.detail: docs/index.html, docs/executive-summary.html and docs/results.html were patched or rewritten by hand while the site generator still emitted the older negative-only content; any later builder run would have discarded the H66-C pages. Fixed by adding docs/data/release-h66c.json, docs/data/executive-summary-sections.json and docs/data/results-h66c-section.json, consumed by the generator, so a rebuild now reproduces the same pages.
